feedback: No race has been run yet for this geometry lineage, so there is no outcome evidence to cite. The points below rest only on the contract physics and the baseline I built. (1) The controller needed the sensor weights set proportional to sensor x with a signal bounded near 2, and kp about 1.2 keeps the wheel differential below the 4095 PWM limit at base_speed 1.6; with a wider wheel track or lower mass the same gains may oscillate less, so I would expect the steering effort to depend mainly on wheel_track and mass. (2) The 0.04 m forward sensor offset gives the controller a short lag, so kd can stay small; if the next race shows steering_oscillation rising at speed, that points to too much forward offset for the current gains rather than to the sensors themselves. (3) The body_width of 0.12 m is well inside the off-track limit (0.06 m floor, tape_half_width + body_width/4 = about 0.0425 m is below the floor), so body_width has no effect on the limit at this value and should not be the first thing changed. Change rules for the next race: if line_loss_events is above zero and max_error is large, widen wheel_track toward 0.15 m (H3) to add turn authority. If steering_oscillation is high and rms_error is low, move the sensors forward (y around 0.06 m) or lower mass toward 0.5 kg to reduce lag. If completion_time is too long without losses, lower mass (H4) before raising base_speed.
requested_changes: Try wheel_track 0.15 m (H3) if the next race shows line_loss_events above zero or max_error rising on the tight bend, since a wider track adds turn authority at the cost of agility; no current evidence confirms this yet.

Try sensor y of 0.06 m (H2) if steering_oscillation is high with low rms_error, since further-forward sensors reduce lag at speed; keep sensor_size at 0.012 unless the signal is noisy across the 25 mm tape.
Try mass 0.5 kg (H4) if completion_time is above about 2.5 s without line losses, since lower mass speeds up acceleration without changing the off-track limit.
